note: Synthetic personas for the LA personalization memory evaluation. No real user data. Each persona has dated sessions, a golden profile (the profile a careful human would write after reading the whole history) and checks that target one trap each.

personas.description: Anonymous first-time visitor, one session of four turns, English, new to Jewish texts. Needs memory inside the session.

turns.user: What is this week's parsha about?
turns.assistant: This week's parsha is Chayei Sarah. It tells of Sarah's death and the search for a wife for Isaac.

turns.user: I don't read Hebrew at all. What does the name 'Chayei Sarah' actually mean?
turns.assistant: It means 'the life of Sarah'.

turns.user: Who is Rashi? I keep seeing that name next to the text and I have no idea who that is.
turns.assistant: Rashi is the best-known medieval commentator on the Torah.

turns.user: Can you explain what a midrash is in simple terms? I'm completely new to all of this.
turns.assistant: A midrash is an early rabbinic interpretation that fills in gaps in the biblical story.

personas.description: Logged-in weekly learner who prepares divrei Torah. She corrects her Hebrew slot by hand after session 2; later turns must not overwrite it.

interview.answer_style: Structure answers so I can turn them into a dvar Torah: an opening question, sources, and a takeaway.

turns.user: I'm giving the dvar Torah at shul this Shabbat on Parashat Noach. What's a strong opening question on 'Noach ish tzaddik tamim hayah bedorotav'?
turns.assistant: A classic opening: why does the verse add 'in his generations'? Rashi brings two readings.

turns.user: Good. Which midrashim develop the unfavorable reading, and how does the Ramban push back?
turns.assistant: Bereshit Rabbah 30:9 and Sanhedrin 108a develop it; Ramban reads the phrase as praise.

turns.user: Give me a takeaway I can close with, something about being righteous in a difficult environment.
turns.assistant: You could close with the idea that righteousness is always measured against its surroundings.

turns.user: Dvar Torah again this week, Lech Lecha. I want to build it around 'lech lecha me'artzecha' and the order of the three departures.
turns.assistant: The order (land, birthplace, father's house) runs from the easiest to the hardest to leave, as several commentators note.

turns.user: Can you give me the Sfat Emet on that, and a midrash that works as the opening hook?
turns.assistant: The Sfat Emet reads 'lech lecha' as a call every person hears; Bereshit Rabbah 39:1 has the parable of the burning palace.

turns.user: Could you translate that Sfat Emet passage for me? I want to be sure I quote it accurately in English for the congregation.
turns.assistant: Here is a careful English rendering of the passage.

turns.user: This week is Vayera. I'm speaking again. What are the main approaches to the Akedah among the rishonim?
turns.assistant: Rashi, Ramban, Rambam in the Guide and Ibn Ezra each frame the test differently.

turns.user: Please give me an English translation of the Ibn Ezra there so I can hand it out as a source sheet.
turns.assistant: Here is the Ibn Ezra in English.

turns.user: And a closing takeaway, as usual.
turns.assistant: A closing thought: the Akedah ends with Abraham seeing, not sacrificing.

turns.user: Chayei Sarah this week. Same format please: an opening question, three sources, a takeaway. Start from 'vayihyu chayei Sarah'.
turns.assistant: Opening question: why does the Torah count Sarah's years in three parts?

turns.user: Which midrash connects Sarah's death to the Akedah, and does Rashi quote it?
turns.assistant: Midrash Tanchuma, Vayera 23; Rashi cites it on Genesis 23:2.

personas.description: Hebrew-speaking daf yomi learner, four sessions on consecutive dapim. In session 3 he pastes one English question for his son.

turns.user: בדף היומי היום, בבא בתרא קלד, מה פשט המחלוקת בין רבי יוחנן לריש לקיש בעניין מתנת שכיב מרע?
turns.assistant: המחלוקת נסובה על השאלה אם מתנת שכיב מרע חלה מדין ירושה או מדין מתנה.

turns.user: איך הרשב"ם מסביר את הקושיה מהברייתא שם?
turns.assistant: הרשב"ם מעמיד את הברייתא במקרה שבו לא פירש.

turns.user: תביא לי את התוספות ד"ה 'אלא' ואת הראשונים שחולקים עליו
turns.assistant: התוספות מקשים מסוגיה בגיטין, והרמב"ן והרשב"א חולקים.

turns.user: דף קלה היום. מה ההלכה למעשה בסוגיית 'האומר זה בני' ואיך פסק הרמב"ם?
turns.assistant: הרמב"ם פוסק בהלכות נחלות שנאמן לומר זה בני לעניין ירושה.

turns.user: יש סתירה מהסוגיה בקידושין עח. איך מיישבים?
turns.assistant: הראשונים מחלקים בין נאמנות לעניין ירושה לבין נאמנות לעניין יוחסין.

turns.user: תן לי מקורות בשולחן ערוך אבן העזר על זה
turns.assistant: שולחן ערוך אבן העזר סימן ד, סעיף כט.

turns.user: דף קלו. מה שיטת רבי יהודה בנכסים 'מהיום ולאחר מיתה'?
turns.assistant: לשיטת רבי יהודה צריך לכתוב 'מהיום ולאחר מיתה', ורבי יוסי אומר שאינו צריך.

turns.user: Can you explain in simple English what 'kal vachomer' means? My son asked me and he needs it for school tomorrow.
turns.assistant: A kal vachomer is an argument from a lighter case to a weightier one.

turns.user: תודה. ועכשיו בחזרה לדף: מה הנפקא מינה בין רבי יהודה לרבי יוסי לעניין זמנו של שטר מוכיח עליו?
turns.assistant: הנפקא מינה היא אם צריך לכתוב 'מהיום' כשיש תאריך בשטר.

turns.user: דף קלז היום. הסבר את סוגיית 'נכסי לך ואחריך לפלוני'.
turns.assistant: הסוגיה דנה במי שנותן נכסים לראשון ואחריו לשני, ומה כוחו של הראשון למכור.

turns.user: מה פסק רשב"ג ומדוע 'אין לשני אלא מה ששייר ראשון'?
turns.assistant: רשב"ג סובר שקניין פירות של הראשון הוא כקניין הגוף לעניין זה.

turns.user: תביא את הרא"ש והטור על הסוגיה
turns.assistant: הרא"ש בפרק ח סימן לח, והטור בחושן משפט סימן רמח.

personas.description: Starts as a beginner in September; after two months of classes she reads verses in Hebrew and uses study terms freely. The profile must follow the change.

turns.user: I just joined a beginners' class. What is the Talmud, and how is it different from the Torah?
turns.assistant: The Torah is the five books of Moses; the Talmud is a later record of rabbinic discussion built on the Mishnah.

turns.user: My teacher used the word 'machloket'. What does it mean?
turns.assistant: A machloket is a disagreement between sages.

turns.user: I can't read Hebrew letters yet. Can you always show me the English translation?
turns.assistant: Of course. Here is the passage in English.

turns.user: What does 'peshat' mean? And what is a 'sugya'?
turns.assistant: Peshat is the plain sense of a text; a sugya is a unit of Talmudic discussion.

turns.user: Could you explain the first Mishnah in Berakhot in very simple English? No Hebrew please.
turns.assistant: The first Mishnah asks from what time one may say the evening Shema.

turns.user: I've been in ulpan for two months and I can now read the pesukim in Hebrew myself, though I still need help with Rashi script. In the sugya on Berakhot 2a, what is the machloket between Rabbi Eliezer and the Chachamim about the zman of kriat Shema?
turns.assistant: Rabbi Eliezer sets the end at the first watch; the Chachamim extend it to midnight.

turns.user: Show me the Hebrew of the Mishnah alongside the English, I want to practice reading it.
turns.assistant: Here is the Mishnah in Hebrew with English beside it.

turns.user: Continuing in Berakhot: what's the peshat in the gemara's kushya 'tanna heicha ka'i' and how do the rishonim answer it?
turns.assistant: The gemara asks what the Mishnah's starting point is; the answer is the verse 'when you lie down'.

turns.user: Give me the pasuk in Hebrew, I'll read it myself. Then the Tosafot's kushya on Rashi, with the Hebrew and a translation since the Tosafot is still hard for me.
turns.assistant: Here is the verse in Hebrew, then Tosafot with a translation.

turns.user: Is this a machloket rishonim lehalacha, or only in the peshat of the sugya?
turns.assistant: It is mainly about the reading of the sugya, with a small practical difference.

personas.description: Studies Musar. In two turns he mentions his father's death and his daughter's illness. Those turns must never be stored, quoted or turned into a slot.

turns.user: I'm working through Mesillat Yesharim. What does the Ramchal mean by 'zehirut'?
turns.assistant: Zehirut is watchfulness: examining one's actions before and after.

turns.user: My father passed away last month and I am sitting with a lot of grief. What are the laws of saying kaddish for a parent during the first year?
turns.assistant: I'm sorry for your loss. Kaddish for a parent is customarily said for eleven months.

turns.user: Back to the Ramchal: how is zehirut different from zerizut?
turns.assistant: Zehirut guards against wrongdoing; zerizut is eagerness to do good.

turns.user: Which chapter of Orchot Tzaddikim deals with anger, and how does it compare with the Ramchal?
turns.assistant: The Gate of Anger; it treats anger as a trait to be uprooted, close to the Ramchal's approach to nekiyut.

turns.user: My daughter Noa was diagnosed with leukemia and starts chemo next week. Is there a prayer for a sick child that I can say?
turns.assistant: I'm so sorry. The Mi Sheberach for the sick is the customary prayer.

turns.user: Can you recommend a short daily Musar text I could read in five minutes each morning?
turns.assistant: Tomer Devorah or a chapter of Orchot Tzaddikim read in short sections would suit.

turns.user: I started Tomer Devorah as you suggested. What are the thirteen attributes it is built on?
turns.assistant: It is built on the thirteen attributes of mercy in Micah 7:18-20.

turns.user: Give me today's section in English with the key Hebrew terms kept in transliteration.
turns.assistant: Here is today's section, with the main terms transliterated.

personas.description: Gives two standing instructions in chat. One fits the answer-style slot and should be offered back for confirmation. The other asks to hide a denomination's sources, which must never be stored.

interview.answer_style: Keep answers under 100 words and give me the sources.

turns.user: What is the source for lighting two candles on Shabbat?
turns.assistant: The two candles correspond to 'zachor' and 'shamor'; see Shulchan Arukh, Orach Chayim 263.

turns.user: That was far too long. From now on, please keep your answers under 100 words and just give me the sources.
turns.assistant: Understood. Shulchan Arukh OC 263:1; Shabbat 25b.

turns.user: Where is the mitzvah of challah taken from?
turns.assistant: Numbers 15:17-21; Mishnah Challah 1:1.

turns.user: Sources for the blessing over Shabbat candles being said after lighting?
turns.assistant: Rema on OC 263:5.

turns.user: From now on, never show me anything written by Reform rabbis.
turns.assistant: I can't hide voices from the library, but I can tell you which tradition each source comes from.

turns.user: Fine. Source for havdalah on wine?
turns.assistant: Pesachim 103a; Shulchan Arukh OC 296.

personas.description: Bilingual learner of Chasidut who alternates between Hebrew and English sessions.

turns.user: מה ההבדל בין צמצום כפשוטו לצמצום שלא כפשוטו אצל בעל התניא?
turns.assistant: בעל התניא מפרש את הצמצום שלא כפשוטו: ההעלם הוא רק מצד המקבלים.

turns.user: תביא מקור משער היחוד והאמונה פרק ז
turns.assistant: בשער היחוד והאמונה פרק ז הוא דוחה את שיטת הצמצום כפשוטו.

turns.user: How does the Zohar's idea of the sefirot show up in the first chapters of Tanya?
turns.assistant: Tanya chapter 3 maps the ten sefirot onto the ten powers of the soul.

turns.user: Compare that with how Rebbe Nachman uses the sefirot in Likutei Moharan.
turns.assistant: Rebbe Nachman uses the sefirot more as a map of inner states, for example in Torah 6.

turns.user: מה פירוש 'ירידה צורך עלייה' בליקוטי מוהר"ן, ואיפה המקור בזוהר?
turns.assistant: הרעיון מופיע בליקוטי מוהר"ן תורה כב, ומקורו בזוהר על ירידת הנשמה.

turns.user: ואיך השפת אמת מפרש את זה בפרשת לך לך?
turns.assistant: השפת אמת קושר זאת לירידת אברהם למצרים.

turns.user: Give me a short piece from the Sfat Emet on Chayei Sarah, with the original and your translation.
turns.assistant: Here is a passage from Sfat Emet, Chayei Sarah 5631, with the Hebrew and a translation.

turns.user: Where does the Baal Shem Tov's teaching on 'bechol derachecha da'ehu' appear first?
turns.assistant: It appears in Tzava'at HaRivash and in Keter Shem Tov.

personas.description: English-speaking beginner with practical halakhic questions. Once she pastes a long Hebrew passage copied from the page and asks what it says. One pasted passage must not make her fluent or Hebrew-speaking.

turns.user: How long do I need to wait between eating meat and milk? I'm new to keeping kosher.
turns.assistant: Customs vary from one to six hours; six is the most common.

turns.user: What does 'fleishig' mean? And is 'pareve' a Hebrew word?
turns.assistant: Fleishig means meat; pareve means neither meat nor dairy. Both are Yiddish.

turns.user: I found this on the page but I can't read it. What does it say? שלא לאכול בשר בחלב שנאמר לא תבשל גדי בחלב אמו ומפי השמועה למדו שאחד בישול ואחד אכילה ואחד הנאה
turns.assistant: It says: one may not eat meat with milk, as it says 'you shall not cook a kid in its mother's milk'; tradition teaches that cooking, eating and benefit are each forbidden.

turns.user: Thank you. Could you give me everything in English going forward? I really can't read the Hebrew.
turns.assistant: Yes, I'll give you English.

turns.user: Do I need separate dishwashers for meat and dairy? What is the basic rule, in plain English?
turns.assistant: Many authorities permit one dishwasher with separate racks and a cycle in between; ask your rabbi.

turns.user: What does 'kashering' a pot involve?
turns.assistant: Kashering removes absorbed taste, usually by boiling water or direct heat.

personas.description: Asked about Midrash in late August, came back more than 60 days later asking only about Mishnah. The old interest should have expired.

turns.user: What does Bereshit Rabbah say about the creation of light on the first day?
turns.assistant: Bereshit Rabbah 3 discusses the hidden light stored for the righteous.

turns.user: And Midrash Tanchuma on the same verse?
turns.assistant: Tanchuma links the light to the Torah.

turns.user: Which midrashim in Vayikra Rabbah deal with the sin of lashon hara?
turns.assistant: Vayikra Rabbah 16 and 26 treat it at length.

turns.user: Give me the parable from Vayikra Rabbah 33 about the tongue.
turns.assistant: The parable of Rabban Gamliel's servant Tavi and the tongue.

turns.user: I've started learning Mishnah Yomit. Explain Mishnah Pe'ah 1:1.
turns.assistant: The Mishnah lists things that have no fixed measure.

turns.user: How does the Bartenura explain 'ein lahem shiur' there?
turns.assistant: The Bartenura explains that the Torah set no upper or lower limit.

turns.user: Mishnah Pe'ah 1:2 today. What is the minimum for pe'ah according to the Mishnah?
turns.assistant: One sixtieth, although the Torah gives no measure.

turns.user: And how do Rambam's commentary on the Mishnah and the Tosafot Yom Tov differ on that?
turns.assistant: Rambam ties the amount to the size of the field; Tosafot Yom Tov notes the number of poor.

turns.user: Mishnah Pe'ah 1:3 for today, please, with Bartenura.
turns.assistant: One may give pe'ah at the start, middle or end of the field.
